uml-canvas.js is Atlas's pre-built UML class-diagram canvas: diagram-js plus the
Atlas-owned renderer, rules and viewer for the information model's notation
(ADR-draft-class-canvas-on-diagram-js).

It contains:

  - diagram-js@15.26.0
  - the Atlas-owned UML class renderer, subset-driven rules provider and
    ClassCanvas in src/index.js

Unlike the ArchiMate canvas beside it, this one edits locally. That canvas never
creates anything, because the server owns the document and the view is re-read; an
information model is a working copy with an explicit Save, which is what lets
somebody draw three classes and two relationships and then decide, and what makes an
undo stack mean anything. So create, connect, move and delete are permitted here —
and the rules still refuse whatever the served subset refuses, at the point of
drawing rather than at the point of writing.

There is a second copy of diagram-js in this binary: the ArchiMate bundle carries
its own. Merging the two into one bundle that exports both viewers is the named
follow-up in the record above; it was left out of the change that created this file
so that change would not touch Panorama's shipped canvas.

diagram-js and its bundled dependencies are MIT licensed (see LICENSE). The Atlas
renderer and rules remain part of Atlas. Only the output is loaded at runtime: Atlas
remains a single, buildless, offline-capable binary (ADR-0012).

Do not edit uml-canvas.js by hand. To rebuild:

  npm install --no-save --no-package-lock diagram-js@15.26.0 esbuild@0.25.9
  npx esbuild api/web/vendor/uml/src/index.js --bundle --format=iife \
    --global-name=AtlasUml --minify --legal-comments=none \
    --outfile=api/web/vendor/uml/uml-canvas.js
  cp node_modules/diagram-js/assets/diagram-js.css \
    api/web/vendor/uml/diagram-js.css
